To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

prenatal treatment with CO MCFA in pregnant does, combined with postnatal treatment of their kids, resulted in reduced CH4 production by the rumen microbiome of goat kids, which was associated with reduced milk replacer intake, reduced BW, and altered rumen papillate morphology.
a combination of prenatal plus postnatal treatment with CO MCFA reduced CH4 emissions in vitro in early life, but effects on in vivo CH4 emissions and rumen microbiome were transient.

prenatal and postnatal treatment with medium chain fatty acids from coconut oil in early life has the potential to reduce CH4 production in vitro, but this effect was transient and did not persist after weaning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hypothesis that early life intervention with CO MCFA is more successful than in the adult animal.
the hypothesis that prenatal and postnatal treatment with CO MCFA can reduce CH4 production in goat kids.

the potential of prenatal and postnatal CO MCFA treatment to alter rumen fermentation in goat kids and the associated rumen microbiota in the short term and the consequences for CH4 production and growth performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

prenatal and postnatal supplementation with CO MCFA during the first 11 wk of life has the potential to reduce in vitro methane emissions, which was accompanied by a lower rumen microbial activity and lower rumen papillar dimensions.

prenatal treatment with CO MCFA during late gestation in goats, followed by postnatal treatment with CO MC FA until weaning, resulted in lower CH4 production and a lower CH4 yield per tVFA produced at 4 wk, but these effects were only transient.

prenatal and postnatal treatment with CO MCFA in early life influences rumen papillar development until 4 mo after supplementation, but effects on in-vitro methane emissions and the microbiota were transient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prenatal and postnatal treatment with CO MCFA in goats has potential to reduce CH4 emissions.
prenatal and/or post-natal treatment with CO MCFA in early life has the potential to influence CH4 production in goat kids, but this effect is transient.
the prenatal and postnatal CO MCFA supplementation in goat kids had an influence on rumen papillate development and on in vitro fermentation parameters at 4 wk of age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
prenatal and postnatal CO MCFA supplementation in goats has the potential to reduce CH4 production in vitro in the first 2 mo of life.
prenatal and/or postpartum treatment with MCFA has the potential to influence the CH4 production of goat kids in vitro, but this effect is transient.
a combination of prenatal (D+K+ kids) and postnatal (K+ kids) treatment with coconut medium-chain fatty acids has potential to lower methane production of goat kids.
